abstract: Maintains radar coverage records and automated identification transponder monitoring logs
system_message:
You are the Vessel Traffic Surveillance Director (VTS), responsible for maintaining radar coverage records, automated identification transponder monitoring logs, and coastal VHF relay reliability assessments across candidate transit corridors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Coastal VHF relay reliability（COMM）
information_points.content:
VTS-COMM-8SX：For the Vaigach Strait Mid-Channel Route, the coastal VHF relay performance audit indicates an emergency radio channel uptime of 100% across maritime distress and calling channel 16 repeating towers over the preceding thirty calendar days.
VTS-COMM-4LY：For the Novaya Zemlya Inshore Corridor, the coastal VHF relay performance audit indicates an emergency radio channel uptime of 95% across maritime distress and calling channel 16 repeating towers over the preceding thirty calendar days.
VTS-COMM-WSE：For the Pechora Sound Southern Passage, the coastal VHF relay performance audit indicates an emergency radio channel uptime of 98% across maritime distress and calling channel 16 repeating towers over the preceding thirty calendar days.

information_points.title: Maintains radar coverage records and automated identification transponder monitoring logs（RADR）
information_points.content:
VTS-RADR-7IJ：For the Pechora Sound Southern Passage routing track line, shore-based radar and automatic identification system line-of-sight provides continuous coastal radar tracking coverage across the entire corridor without blind sectors.
VTS-RADR-T2P：For the Novaya Zemlya Inshore Corridor routing track line, shore-based radar and automatic identification system line-of-sight does not provide continuous coastal radar tracking coverage across the entire corridor.
VTS-RADR-65K：For the Vaigach Strait Mid-Channel Route routing track line, shore-based radar and automatic identification system line-of-sight provides continuous coastal radar tracking coverage across the entire corridor without blind sectors.
